stories.title: Lawsuit over blocked server farm could reshape property taxes, power costs
stories.dek: A data-center developer has filed suit against an Oakland County municipality after local officials blocked or delayed its project. The lawsuit puts the fight over land use, tax revenue, and power demand directly in front of a judge. Oakland County residents will feel the outcome in their electric bills and property taxes whether the project is approved or killed.
stories.source_title: Data-center developer sues Oakland County city - mlive.com

stories.title: Michigan suburb blocks server farms another year amid power, water worries
stories.dek: Rochester Hills has prolonged its temporary ban on new data-center proposals. The extension keeps large-scale projects from moving forward while the city studies power, water, and noise impacts. Residents within 30 miles will see whether the pause becomes permanent policy or gives way to tax-generating campuses.
stories.source_title: Rochester Hills extends data center moratorium - detroitnews.com

stories.title: Consumers Energy lines spark farm backlash across Michigan
stories.dek: New transmission projects tied to data-center power needs are cutting through rural land and drawing protests. Farmers worry about lost acreage, health effects, and depressed property values. The utility says the upgrades are required to meet surging electricity demand from AI facilities.
stories.source_title: How Consumers Energy Turns Michigan Farm Communities Upside Down - Michigan Enjoyer

stories.title: Morley residents halt data center talks after 170 pack the room
stories.dek: A packed crowd in Morley forced officials to postpone any discussion of a proposed data facility. Residents voiced immediate concerns over power demand, noise, and water use in the rural township. The delay gives locals more time to organize before the project advances.
stories.source_title: Crowd of roughly 170 forces Morley to postpone meeting on data facility - Big Rapids Pioneer

stories.title: Detroit data centers capped at small scale under new rules
stories.dek: City policy keeps new facilities from growing into massive power users that strain local grids. Residents avoid the heavy electricity rate hikes and noise seen in other states. The limit protects neighborhood character while still allowing limited tech growth.
stories.source_title: 🤖 Detroit’s data centers to stay small - Outlier Media

stories.title: Detroit Grid Too Weak for Hyperscale Data Centers, DTE Tells Planners
stories.dek: Six small centers already run in the city, but council members and residents now demand a moratorium on bigger ones until impact studies are done.

stories.title: Mount Pleasant data center keeps Wisconsin-rejected power plant clause
stories.dek: The contract for the Mount Pleasant project still includes a power plant provision already struck down by Wisconsin regulators. Residents face the risk of higher local energy costs if the plant moves forward to serve the data center. The deal shows how out-of-state regulatory fights can directly shape Michigan power bills.
stories.source_title: Mount Pleasant data center contract retains power plant provision struck down by Wisconsin regulators - PBS Wisconsin

stories.title: Lowell pushes data center rules back by months
stories.dek: Officials in Lowell say new zoning and permitting standards for data centers will not be ready for several more months. Until then, any proposals could move forward under current weak rules. Kent County residents have little say on power and water demands until the ordinance is finished.
stories.source_title: Lowell data center regulations still months away, officials say - MLive.com

stories.title: Whitehall Township drafts first data center rules
stories.dek: Whitehall Township supervisors reviewed a new ordinance aimed at controlling data center construction. The rules would set limits on size, noise and power use in a rural area. Muskegon County residents could see changes in taxes and grid strain depending on what passes.
stories.source_title: Whitehall Township takes first look at proposed data center ordinance - WFMZ.com

stories.title: Kalamazoo weighs year-long freeze on new data centers
stories.dek: City leaders will debate a moratorium at their next meeting that would block proposals while officials study power and water demands. Residents 30 miles away could see higher electric rates if large projects move forward unchecked. The pause would give local officials time to write rules before any campus breaks ground.
stories.source_title: Kalamazoo city leaders to consider data center moratorium at next meeting - WOODTV.com

stories.title: U.P. locals team with comedian to block AI data centers
stories.dek: Residents in Michigan's Upper Peninsula are pushing back against proposed AI data centers that could strain local power grids and water supplies. Comedian Charlie Berens is amplifying their concerns in public opposition efforts. The fight highlights growing pushback in rural Michigan communities over energy demands from big tech projects.
stories.source_title: Midwestern comedian Charlie Berens joins U.P. residents to oppose A.I. data centers - myupnow.com

national.title: Data centers advance rapidly as regulators scramble for rules
national.dek: Across the U.S., officials race to impose guardrails on power-hungry facilities while communities push back on incentives and impacts.
